findings.summary: The named Goal B/E docs still claim the default configuration/output fingerprints are unchanged, contradicting the task's own version advance, the task acceptance criterion, and the adjacent 12.4 correction.
findings.detail: docs/architecture.md section 9 (lines ~1228-1242), docs/data-model.md 3.6 (lines ~592-602), and docs/data-model.md 3.12 (lines ~939-949) state that the V1 default is identity-neutral, 'so the default configuration and output fingerprints are unchanged' / 'an unchanged configuration keeps the V1 identity'. The task 12.4 sentence appended immediately after each of these states that the default output fingerprints 'advance with the renderer version'. Both cannot be true. After the coordinated advance, RendererConfigurationFingerprint.Compute() hashes rendererConfigurationSchemaVersion (now 2, was 1) at RendererConfigurationFingerprint.cs:38, and RenderFingerprint.ComputeOutputFingerprint hashes rendererVersion (now 3, was 2) at RenderFingerprint.cs:34 plus the configuration fingerprint at :40, so the default configuration and output fingerprints DO change; the observed git diff already shows every one of the 9 existing manifest OutputFingerprint values changed while only the PNG bytes are unchanged. The stale sentence also directly contradicts the acceptance criterion 'the renderer configuration fingerprint changes'. Only the PNG bytes (visual output) are unchanged; the fingerprints are not. The placement values themselves remain identity-neutral (RendererConfigurationFingerprint.cs:66-76 and RenderFingerprint.cs:69-80 append nothing for the default), which is the accurate way to phrase it.

The goldens were regenerated, so one accepted closure path is satisfied, but the absolute pin remains the native-Skia-guarded golden comparison: in the default suite the golden theory is reported as a single skip (SkiaNativeTheoryAttribute sets Skip), so no unguarded test absolutely pins the default output/configuration fingerprint against a hardcoded value. The existing unguarded tests remain relative (RenderedFingerprintTests:179-185 asserts an explicit-default policy equals the default; RendererConfigurationTests:521-550 and :553+ assert sensitivity/normalization). This is a test-strength residual, not a functional defect (production is identity-neutral by construction), and it is legitimately owned by the native golden path; flagging it so the task-quality reviewer evaluates closure rather than assuming it.
